This script prepares the data of the survey experiment before the 2024 Saxon state election.
It follows `21_federal_data_preparation.Rmd` and writes three files to `data/processed/`, which `32_saxony_descriptives.Rmd` reads:

- `results_official_saxony.rdata`: the official list-vote result, the benchmark of all accuracy measures,
- `data_saxony.rdata`: one row per respondent (first participation only) with all variables of the analyses,
- `data_saxony_long.rdata`: one row per respondent and party with the expected vote share and the forecast error.


# Official Election Result

List-vote shares of the 2024 Saxon state election (Table 1), read from the final result of the Statistisches Landesamt Sachsen (`data/input/results/`).
The file has one row per area. The state-level row (`Ebene == "SN"`) is used, and the list-vote columns end in `_2`.
The eight parties asked about in the survey keep their name, all other parties form *Others*.
Shares are in % of the valid list votes and add up to 100.

```{r results_official_saxony}
votes_saxony <- read_excel("data/input/results/statistik-sachsen_LW24_endgErgebniss.xlsx",
  sheet = "LW24_endgErgebnisse_SN&WK"
) %>%
  filter(Ebene == "SN") %>% # state-level row
  select(ends_with("_2")) %>% # "_2" = list votes
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "party_raw", values_to = "votes")

valid_votes_saxony <- votes_saxony %>%
  filter(str_detect(party_raw, "^g.*ltige_2$")) %>% # "gültige_2" = valid list votes
  pull(votes)

results_official_saxony <- votes_saxony %>%
  filter(!str_detect(party_raw, "ltige_2$")) %>% # without valid and invalid votes
  mutate(party = case_when( # parties in the survey, all others combined
    party_raw == "CDU_2" ~ "CDU",
    party_raw == "AfD_2" ~ "AfD",
    party_raw == "DIE LINKE_2" ~ "Left",
    str_detect(party_raw, "^GR") ~ "Greens",
    party_raw == "SPD_2" ~ "SPD",
    party_raw == "FDP_2" ~ "FDP",
    str_detect(party_raw, "^FREIE W") ~ "Free Voters",
    party_raw == "BSW_2" ~ "BSW",
    TRUE ~ "Others"
  )) %>%
  group_by(party) %>%
  summarize(result_official = sum(votes) / valid_votes_saxony * 100, .groups = "drop") # share of valid list votes in %
rm(votes_saxony, valid_votes_saxony)

results_official_saxony

save(results_official_saxony, file = "data/processed/results_official_saxony.rdata")
```


# Survey Data

## Sample

```{r load}
load("data/input/survey/survey_saxony.rdata")

data_saxony <- survey_saxony %>%
  mutate(
    treatment = factor(
      group,
      levels = c("control", "treatment"),
      labels = c("Control", "Treatment (500)")
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-group) %>%
  mutate(pid = case_when(
    is.na(pid) ~ NA_character_,
    pid == "CDU" ~ "CDU",
    pid == "AfD" ~ "AfD",
    pid == "DIE LINKE" ~ "Left",
    pid == "GRÜNE" ~ "Greens",
    pid == "SPD" ~ "SPD",
    pid == "FDP" ~ "FDP",
    pid == "BSW" ~ "BSW",
    pid == "Keine Partei" ~ "none",
    TRUE ~ "other" # "Andere Partei"
  )) %>%
  # Free Voters identifiers from the open answer
  mutate(pid = if_else(pid == "other" & !is.na(pid_other) & pid_other == "FREIE WÄHLER", "Free Voters", pid))

data_saxony %>% count(treatment)
data_saxony %>% count(source)
data_saxony %>% count(pid)
rm(survey_saxony)
```

## Variables

Recodes of the variables used in the models:

- `lead_time`: days between the interview and the election day (1 September 2024), used as survey date fixed effects,
- `turnout_int_dummy`: intends to vote (certain to vote or already voted by mail),
- `recruit`: recruitment channel, online access panel (OAP) or social media (SM),
- `zs_int`: vote intention with the party names of the long data (other parties and invalid votes are missing),

The cross table checks the turnout dummy against the original answers.

```{r recodes}
data_saxony <- data_saxony %>%
  mutate(
    # Days before the election (survey date fixed effects), computed in 01_create_replication_data.R
    lead_time = as_factor(lead_time),
    turnout_int = factor(turnout_int, levels = rev(levels(turnout_int))),
    # Turnout intention: certain to vote or already voted by mail
    turnout_int_dummy = case_when(
      turnout_int %in% c("bestimmt zur Wahl gehen", "ich habe bereits Briefwahl gemacht") ~ "ja",
      TRUE ~ "nein"
    ),
    turnout_int_dummy = factor(turnout_int_dummy, levels = c("nein", "ja")),
    # Recruitment channel: online access panel or social media
    recruit = if_else(str_detect(source, "bilendi"), "OAP", "SM"),
    # Vote intention with the party names of the long data
    # Other parties and invalid votes are NA
    zs_int = case_when(
      list_vote_int_major %in% c("Eine andere Partei", "Ich werden ungültig wählen.") ~ NA_character_,
      list_vote_int_major == "GRÜNE" ~ "Greens",
      list_vote_int_major == "DIE LINKE" ~ "Left",
      list_vote_int_major == "FREIE WÄHLER" ~ "Free Voters",
      list_vote_int_major %in% c("CDU", "CSU") ~ "CDU",
      TRUE ~ as.character(list_vote_int_major)
    )
  ) %>%
  set_variable_labels(
    lead_time         = "Number of days before the election the interview took place",
    turnout_int_dummy = "Turnout intention dummy (certain to vote or mail = yes)",
    recruit           = "Recruitment: OAP = online access panel, SM = social media"
  )

data_saxony %>%
  count(turnout_int, turnout_int_dummy) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = turnout_int_dummy, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
data_saxony %>% count(recruit)
```

The sample composition table (Table B.4) compares the sample with the electorate.
For this, age, vote intention, gender, education and turnout intention are grouped into the categories of the official statistics, with English labels.
Respondents who answered "diverse" are counted as men (Men*), as in the representative electoral statistics.
The tables show the distribution of each recoded variable.

```{r recodes_sample_composition}
data_saxony <- data_saxony %>%
  mutate(
    age_group = case_when(
      age < 30 ~ "18-29",
      age >= 30 & age < 40 ~ "30-39",
      age >= 40 & age < 50 ~ "40-49",
      age >= 50 & age < 60 ~ "50-59",
      age >= 60 ~ "60+",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    list_vote_int_eng = case_when(
      list_vote_int_major %in% c("Eine andere Partei", "Ich werden ungültig wählen.") ~ "Other",
      list_vote_int_major == "GRÜNE" ~ "Greens",
      list_vote_int_major == "DIE LINKE" ~ "Left",
      list_vote_int_major == "FREIE WÄHLER" ~ "Free Voters",
      TRUE ~ list_vote_int_major
    ),
    list_vote_int_eng = factor(list_vote_int_eng,
      levels = c("AfD", "Greens", "BSW", "CDU", "FDP", "Left", "SPD", "Free Voters", "Other")
    ),
    gender_eng = case_when(
      gender == "Weiblich" ~ "Women",
      gender == "Männlich" ~ "Men",
      gender == "Divers" ~ "Diverse",
      TRUE ~ gender
    ),
    # Diverse counted as men (Men*)
    gender_eng2 = if_else(gender_eng == "Diverse", "Men", gender_eng),
    education_eng = case_when(
      education %in% c(
        "Schule beendet ohne Abschluss",
        "Hauptschulabschluss, Volksschulabschluss, Abschluss der polytechnischen Oberschule 8. oder 9. Klasse"
      ) ~ "Low",
      education %in% c(
        "Realschulabschluss, Mittlere Reife, Fachschulreife oder Abschluss der polytechnischen Oberschule 10. Klasse"
      ) ~ "Medium",
      education == "Bin noch Schüler/in" ~ "Still in School",
      education == "Anderen Schulabschluss, und zwar:" ~ NA,
      education %in% c(
        "Fachhochschulreife (Abschluss einer Fachoberschule etc.)",
        "Abitur bzw. erweiterte Oberschule mit Abschluss 12. Klasse (Hochschulreife)"
      ) ~ "High",
      TRUE ~ education
    ),
    education_eng = factor(education_eng,
      levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High", "Still in School")
    ),
    turnout_int_eng = case_when(
      turnout_int_dummy == "nein" ~ "No",
      turnout_int_dummy == "ja" ~ "Yes",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

data_saxony %>% count(age_group)
data_saxony %>% count(gender_eng2)
data_saxony %>% count(education_eng)
data_saxony %>% count(turnout_int_eng)
data_saxony %>% count(list_vote_int_eng)
```

## Response Times

The survey file contains the same response times as the federal data (in seconds):

- the time spent on the page of the expectation item (`t_list_votes_exp_Page_Submit`), the dependent variable of H1 (logged),
- the times of five filler items (birth year, vote intention, eligibility, turnout intention, political interest), from which 32 computes each respondent's baseline speed.

The output summarizes the response time of the expectation item in seconds.

```{r response_times}
time_vars_saxony <- c("t_list_votes_exp_Page_Submit", baseline_speed_vars)

data_saxony <- data_saxony %>%
  # Logged response time (H1)
  mutate(t_list_votes_exp_Page_Submit_log = log(t_list_votes_exp_Page_Submit))

data_saxony %>%
  summarize(
    n_missing = sum(is.na(t_list_votes_exp_Page_Submit)),
    min = min(t_list_votes_exp_Page_Submit, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(t_list_votes_exp_Page_Submit, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean = mean(t_list_votes_exp_Page_Submit, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(t_list_votes_exp_Page_Submit, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  print_values(digits = 1) # helper
```

## Vote Share Expectations (Long Data)

Respondents gave their expected vote share for eight parties and *Others* on sliders.
The wide data are reshaped to one row per respondent and party, and the official result of the party is joined.
The forecast error is the expected minus the actual vote share (`list_votes_exp_diff`, in percentage points).
Positive values mean the party was overestimated.
The H3 models use these long data.
The output shows the rows of one respondent.

```{r long}
list_votes_exp_vars_saxony <- c(
  "CDU"         = "list_votes_exp_cdu",
  "AfD"         = "list_votes_exp_afd",
  "Left"        = "list_votes_exp_linke",
  "Greens"      = "list_votes_exp_gruene",
  "SPD"         = "list_votes_exp_spd",
  "FDP"         = "list_votes_exp_fdp",
  "BSW"         = "list_votes_exp_bsw",
  "Free Voters" = "list_votes_exp_fw",
  "Others"      = "list_votes_exp_other"
)

data_saxony_long <- data_saxony %>%
  select(
    ResponseId, id_unique, treatment, lead_time,
    age, gender, education,
    list_vote_int_major, starts_with("ptv_"), pid,
    all_of(list_votes_exp_vars_saxony)
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(names(list_votes_exp_vars_saxony)),
    names_to = "party",
    values_to = "list_votes_exp"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    results_official_saxony %>% rename(list_votes_result = result_official),
    by = "party"
  ) %>%
  mutate(list_votes_exp_diff = list_votes_exp - list_votes_result) %>%
  relocate(party, list_votes_exp, list_votes_result, list_votes_exp_diff, .after = id_unique)

data_saxony_long %>%
  filter(ResponseId == first(ResponseId)) %>%
  select(party, list_votes_exp, list_votes_result, list_votes_exp_diff) %>%
  print_values() # helper
```

## Individual Accuracy (MAE, RMSE)

The accuracy of each respondent's expectations, the dependent variable of H2:
the mean absolute error (MAE) and, as a robustness check, the root mean squared error (RMSE) of the forecast errors over the nine categories (eight parties and *Others*).
Lower values mean more accurate expectations.

```{r accuracy}
accuracy_saxony <- data_saxony_long %>%
  group_by(ResponseId) %>%
  summarize(
    list_votes_exp_mae  = mean(abs(list_votes_exp_diff)),
    list_votes_exp_rmse = sqrt(mean(list_votes_exp_diff^2)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

data_saxony <- data_saxony %>%
  left_join(accuracy_saxony, by = "ResponseId") %>%
  set_variable_labels(
    list_votes_exp_mae  = "MAE List Vote Expectations",
    list_votes_exp_rmse = "RMSE List Vote Expectations"
  )

data_saxony %>%
  summarize(across(c(list_votes_exp_mae, list_votes_exp_rmse), list(mean = mean, sd = sd))) %>%
  print_values() # helper

rm(accuracy_saxony)
```


# Save

Only the variables used later are kept.

```{r save}
data_saxony <- data_saxony %>%
  select(
    # IDs and interview
    ResponseId, id_unique, source, recruit, interview_date, duration, lead_time,
    # Experiment
    treatment, pledge_expectations,
    # Demographics
    age, age_group, gender, gender_eng, gender_eng2,
    education, education_eng,
    # Political variables
    pol_interest, turnout_int, turnout_int_dummy, turnout_int_eng,
    list_vote_int_major, list_vote_int_eng, zs_int, starts_with("ptv_"), pid,
    # Vote share expectations and accuracy
    all_of(unname(list_votes_exp_vars_saxony)),
    list_votes_exp_mae, list_votes_exp_rmse,
    # Response times
    all_of(time_vars_saxony), t_list_votes_exp_Page_Submit_log
  )

save(data_saxony, file = "data/processed/data_saxony.rdata")
save(data_saxony_long, file = "data/processed/data_saxony_long.rdata")
```
